Symptoms: Circular to angular dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings producing a target-board pattern, surrounded by chlorotic yellow halo on older lower leaves.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage Potato, PlantDoc, Kaggle Potato Blight, CPRI Gujarat Field Imagery
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2-M / ConvNeXt Foliar Classifier + U-Net Lesion Segmentation
Diagnostic_Limitations: May resemble brown spot (Alternaria alternata) or late-stage ozone injury; target concentric rings provide strong visual separation.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Bulletin No. 94; SDAU Sardarkrushinagar Potato Pathology Compendium

Symptoms: Rapidly enlarging water-soaked irregular lesions turning purplish-brown/black, delicate white cottony downy fungal sporulation on lower leaf margins under high humidity; necrotic stem lesions; copper-brown dry granular rot on tuber periderm.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage Potato Late Blight, CPRI Late Blight Repository, Mendeley Potato Diseases
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2-M + U-Net Segmentation + RH Weather Cross-Validation
Diagnostic_Limitations: Rapid collapse under cold wet conditions (>90% RH, 10-20°C); stem lesions require high resolution to distinguish from bacterial blackleg.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Disease Management Bulletin; PPQ&S Integrated Pest Management Package for Potato

Symptoms: Hard, superficial, irregular brownish-black sclerotial encrustations resembling dirt particles ('dirt that won't wash off') adhering tightly to tuber skin; brown sunken lesions/cankers on subterranean sprouts and stolons.
Required_Dataset: Kaggle Potato Tuber Diseases, Mendeley Potato Tuber Surface Defects, CPRI Deesa Post-Harvest Collection
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Tuber Surface Defect Detection + Texture Feature Mapping
Diagnostic_Limitations: Surface sclerotia easily mistaken for dry soil clods if tuber unwashed; water-washed tuber photograph mandatory.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Annual Report (Rhizoctonia in Banaskantha Sandy-Loam Soils); SDAU Dept of Plant Pathology

Symptoms: Superficial, raised corky or deeply pitted rough brown stellate lesions with ragged margins on potato tuber skin; leaves and aboveground foliage remain asymptomatic.
Required_Dataset: Mendeley Scab & Defect Dataset, Kaggle Potato Tuber Conditions, Indian Agricultural Research Repositories
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Defect Detection / EfficientNetV2 Tuber Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Distinguishing pitted common scab from powdery scab (Spongospora subterranea) visually requires macro close-up of periderm pustule fringes.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory; AAU Anand Soil Microbiology Bulletins

Symptoms: Small purple-brown raised pimples on tuber surface that rupture to reveal open crater-like pustules filled with golden-brown to dark brown powdery spore balls (cystosori), surrounded by elevated frayed skin edges.
Required_Dataset: EPPO Global Database, Academic Cercozoan Collections, High-res Macro Tuber Defect Images
Detection_Method: High-Resolution Macro Feature Classifier + Edge Raggedness Analysis
Diagnostic_Limitations: Strong visual overlap with Common Scab (Streptomyces); requires close-up macro imaging to detect loose powdery spore balls vs hard corky scab.
Reference_Source: CABI Compendium; ICAR-CPRI Shimla Seed Pathology Manual

Symptoms: Sunken, shriveled, dark brown to black necrotic depressions on tuber skin with concentric wrinkling; internal dry crumbly rot with hollow cavities lined with white, pinkish, or yellow fungal mycelial tufts.
Required_Dataset: Post-Harvest Potato Storage Pathology Datasets, Kaggle Storage Tuber Diseases
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Tuber Surface & Cut-Section Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: External sunken wrinkling detectable; full confirmation of internal dry rot cavity requires cut-surface tuber photo.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Storage Rot Bulletin; Gujarat State Agricultural Marketing Board Advisory

Symptoms: Rapid daylight wilting and flagging of green foliage starting on one branch while leaves remain green; brown discoloration of vascular ring in cut stem and tuber; white bacterial slime oozing from vascular ring when suspended in water.
Required_Dataset: Ralstonia Wilt Academic Repositories, CPRI Bacterial Wilt Field Survey, Kaggle Vascular Wilt
Detection_Method: Multi-Image Diagnostic Flow (Foliar Wilt View + Cut-Stem / Vascular Ring View)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Foliar collapse looks indistinguishable from Verticillium wilt or mechanical root injury; requires cut-stem vascular browning or glass-water bacterial ooze stream test.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Bulletin on Bacterial Wilt; National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS) Strategic Paper

Symptoms: Water-soaked, soft, creamy to tan mushy maceration of tuber tissue turning watery with a sharp, foul putrid fishy odor; periderm remains intact as an empty blister-like skin bag until ruptured.
Required_Dataset: Tuber Post-Harvest Bacterial Rots Dataset, Indian Agricultural Cold-Storage Surveys
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 / EfficientNetV2 Tuber Decomposition Analysis
Diagnostic_Limitations: Easily identified visually once periderm ruptures; odorless early stages can resemble wet rot of Pythium or Phytophthora erythroseptica.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Storage Pathology Manual; AAU Anand Postharvest Entomology & Pathology Guidelines

Symptoms: Inky jet-black, shiny, slimy decay extending upward from decaying seed tuber along lower subterranean stem above soil line; upper leaves roll inward, become chlorotic, stiff, and erect; premature plant collapse.
Required_Dataset: Dickeya & Pectobacterium Field Datasets, Plant Pathology Diagnostic Archive
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Stem Base & Canopy Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Stem base photograph showing soil-stem interface is essential; canopy symptoms alone resemble severe nitrogen deficiency or rhizoctonia stem canker.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Pathology Compendium; European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO)

Symptoms: Upward and inward spoon-shaped rolling of lower leaflets which become leathery, thick, brittle, and papery crisp; chlorosis with pinkish/purple tinge at margins; stunted rigid upright canopy; net necrosis in stored tubers.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage Potato Leaf Roll, CPRI Seed Certification Virus Image Library
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Foliar Texture & Curvature Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Symptom mimicry with severe drought stress, aphid-transmitted toxemia, or rhizoctonia collar girdling; lower leaf brittle texture check needed.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Seed Potato Certification Standards; SDAU Agricultural Research Publications

Symptoms: Vein-clearing, severe systemic chlorotic mottle, mosaic patterning, rugosity, leaf dropping with 'leaf-drop streak' (dead leaves hanging along stem), severe plant stunting; brown ringspot lesions on tubers in PVY-NTN strains.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage, PlantDoc, Kaggle Potato Virus, CPRI Vector-Borne Virus Repository
Detection_Method: ConvNeXt-S / EfficientNetV2 Foliar Mosaic Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Symptoms vary widely according to potato cultivar and virus strain (PVY-O, PVY-N, PVY-NTN); cross-reaction with PVA and PVX.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Deesa Research Station Bulletin; World Potato Congress Pathology Archive

Symptoms: Mild diffuse interveinal mottle or light green variegated mosaic pattern; slight crinkling of leaf margins; often symptomless or masked under high temperatures (>25°C).
Required_Dataset: Academic Potato Virology Archives, Plant Diagnostic Collections
Detection_Method: Fine-Grained Foliar Contrast Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Frequently latent and completely asymptomatic in modern cultivars; severe symptoms only occur when co-infected with PVY ('rugose mosaic').
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Disease Diagnostics Manual; CABI Plantwise Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Very mild or imperceptible foliage mottle, faint deepening of leaf veins, slight downward curling of apical leaves; predominantly asymptomatic in field conditions.
Required_Dataset: Academic Virology Datasets (ELISA/RT-PCR confirmed)
Detection_Method: Out-of-Scope for Autonomous Image CV / Laboratory ELISA Alert
Diagnostic_Limitations: Visually undetectable with reliability in field settings; standard computer vision models produce false positives on mild nutrient deviations; requires DAS-ELISA or RT-PCR.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Virology Division Manual; EPPO Data Sheets on Quarantine Pests

Scientific_Name: Potato Mosaic Virus Complex (PVA / PVM / Mixed)
Symptoms: Irregular patches of alternating light and dark green on leaf laminae, puckered or crinkled leaf surface, wavy leaf margins, reduced leaflet size and general vine vigor.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage Potato, Mendeley Agricultural Imagery, Field Virology Sets
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Mosaic Feature Extraction
Diagnostic_Limitations: Visual symptoms overlap across Potato Virus A, Potato Virus M, and mild PVY; reliable diagnosis reports 'Potato Mosaic Complex' with vector management advisory.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory Bulletin; AAU Anand Entomology and Plant Pathology Reports

Symptoms: Cauliflower-like warty or coral-like tumors and coralloid excrescences developing on tubers, stolons, stem bases, and eyes; green when exposed to light, turning black and rotting at maturity.
Required_Dataset: EPPO Global Quarantine Image Database, National Plant Protection Collections
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Quarantine Tumor Detection / High-Precision Binary Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Notified A1 quarantine pest in India (historically restricted to Darjeeling hills); system must trigger immediate national biosecurity alert upon positive detection.
Reference_Source: Destructive Insects and Pests Act (DIPA 1914, GoI); Directorate of PPQ&S Quarantine Compendium

Symptoms: Light brown to silvery or gray glistening patches on tuber periderm, especially visible when tuber is moistened; surface cells slough off; causes tuber dehydration and flaccidity during cold storage.
Required_Dataset: Post-Harvest Tuber Defect Dataset, University Storage Pathology Sets
Detection_Method: Tuber Periderm Texture & Specular Reflectance Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Very difficult to differentiate visually from Black Dot (Colletotrichum coccodes); microscopic conidiophore examination or moist-chamber incubation recommended.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Storage Pathology Manual; Michigan State University Extension Potato Diseases

Symptoms: Rubbery, spongy decay of tubers beginning at stolon end; dull brown periderm; internal cut tuber flesh turns distinctive salmon-pink within 15-20 minutes of atmospheric air exposure, gradually turning brown then black.
Required_Dataset: Specialized Post-Harvest Tuber Internal Rots Academic Image Sets
Detection_Method: Multi-Temporal Cut-Section Color Transformation Analysis (0 min vs 20 min photo)
Diagnostic_Limitations: External tuber symptoms mimic Pythium leak; internal salmon-pink color reaction upon cutting and oxygen exposure is the definitive diagnostic signature.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Potato Disease Compendium; University of Idaho Extension Potato Pathology

Symptoms: Interveinal yellowing followed by necrosis on lower leaves, frequently beginning on one side of leaf or plant ('one-sided wilt'); premature senescence ('potato early dying syndrome'); light brown vascular vascular discoloration in lower stem.
Required_Dataset: Academic Vascular Wilt Research Datasets, University Crop Pathology Collections
Detection_Method: Out-of-Scope for Definite Visual CV / Vascular Wilt Triage Alert
Diagnostic_Limitations: Visual appearance identical to Fusarium oxysporum wilt, natural senescence, and drought injury; requires laboratory isolation on agar medium or PCR for species confirmation.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Soil Pathology Manual; APS Compendium of Potato Diseases (Stevenson et al.)

Symptoms: Larval blotch mines and windowing in foliar leaves; slender tunneling throughout tuber flesh beneath skin, with entrance holes surrounded by dark powdery larval excrement/frass; rotting under storage.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Insect Pest Dataset, CPRI Deesa Post-Harvest Storage Pest Imagery, Mendeley Tuber Pest Data
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Frass & Tunnel Detection on Tuber / Larval Mine Classifier on Leaves
Diagnostic_Limitations: Tuber damage unmistakable when frass-filled entry holes present; foliar mines must be distinguished from serpentine leaf miner.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Deesa Center Pest Bulletin; Gujarat Agricultural University Entomological Studies

Symptoms: Dense colonies of small pear-shaped green, yellowish, or pinkish soft-bodied insects clustering on abaxial leaf surface and growing tips; leaf curling, crinkling, sticky honeydew secretion, and black sooty mold growth.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Insect Dataset, PlantDoc, Agricultural Pest Kaggle Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Macro Pest Object Detector + Sooty Mold Foliar Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Primary agricultural significance in Gujarat (Deesa) is vectoring PLRV and PVY; requires high-resolution macro imagery to differentiate aphid species.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Seed Vector Aphid Forecasting System; SDAU Entomology Advisory

Symptoms: Tiny chalky-white moth-like insects fluttering around canopy when disturbed; scale-like flat translucent nymphs feeding on leaf undersides; chlorotic leaf stippling, honeydew, vector of Potato Apical Leaf Curl Virus (PALCV).
Required_Dataset: IP102 Whitefly Class, PlantDoc, Gujarat Cotton & Potato Pest Image Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Abaxial Leaf Insect Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Adults fly away upon disturbance; photographing stationary underside nymphs or combining with apical leaf curl foliar pattern provides superior accuracy.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Bulletin on Potato Apical Leaf Curl Geminivirus; AAU Anand Entomology Guidelines

Symptoms: Silvery or bleached epidermal flecking and scratching along leaf veins; tiny black tar-like fecal drops; curling, bronzing, and crinkling of young leaflets; vector of Tomato Spotted Wilt / Groundnut Bud Necrosis Virus.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Thrips Class, Micro-Pest Agricultural Datasets, Kaggle Thrips Damage
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Foliar Feeding Injury & Micro-Pest Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Individual insects are tiny (1 mm); model relies heavily on characteristic silvery foliar scarring and black droplet patterning rather than insect morphology alone.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Entomology Division; SDAU Crop Protection Series

Symptoms: Young seedling stems completely cut off at or just below ground level; severed tender stems dragged into soil; large irregular gouged cavities in shallow-set seed tubers; fat greasy grayish-black caterpillars curled in 'C' shape in soil.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Noctuid Cutworm Datasets, CPRI Field Damage Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Larval & Stem-Severance Damage Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Caterpillar is nocturnal and conceals itself in topsoil during daytime; diagnosis from aboveground severed stem requires user to gently unearth soil near plant base to photograph larva.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory; PPQ&S National IPM Protocol for Solanaceous Crops

Symptoms: Small wedge-shaped pale green insects walking diagonally on leaf undersides; feeding causes downward rolling of leaf margins, yellowing of leaflet tips, and progressive brown triangular margin necrosis ('hopper burn').
Required_Dataset: IP102 Jassid Category, ICAR Pest Repositories, Gujarat Agriculture Leafhopper Library
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Hopper Burn Classifier + YOLOv8 Jassid Nymph Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Hopper burn can be confused with potassium deficiency or moisture scorch; presence of marginal triangular chlorosis and wedge-shaped nymphs confirms identity.
Reference_Source: SDAU Sardarkrushinagar Entomology Department; ICAR-CPRI Deesa Entomological Survey

Scientific_Name: Agriotes spp. / Melanotus spp. (Click beetle larvae)
Symptoms: Neat, clean, cylindrical circular bore holes (1 to 3 mm diameter) drilled deeply into potato tuber flesh; subterranean sprout destruction; hard slender wiry shiny yellow-brown click beetle larvae.
Required_Dataset: Tuber Subterranean Pest Datasets, Academic Soil Arthropod Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Circular Tuber Borehole Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Tuber must be harvested and washed; bore holes look similar to potato tuber moth entry holes, but lack powdery fecal frass plugging.
Reference_Source: CABI Compendium of Soil Insects; ICAR-CPRI Subterranean Pests Review

Symptoms: Prominent pimples, blisters, and warty gall-like swellings over tuber periderm; internal vascular brown flecks; stunted, chlorotic, unthrifty canopy wilting during peak sunshine; severe knot-like galls on roots.
Required_Dataset: Nematode Gall Root Datasets, Mendeley Root Defect Data, CPRI Nematology Image Vault
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Root Galling & Tuber Pimple Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Aboveground canopy symptoms look identical to general drought or root rot; diagnosis requires uprooting the plant and photographing washed roots or pimpled tubers.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Division of Crop Protection (Nematology); AAU Nematology Department Research Bulletins

Symptoms: Numerous tiny round 'shot-hole' perforations eaten into leaf lamina by small, jumping dark beetles; subterranean white grubs chew shallow winding grooves, scars, and channels into tuber skin.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Flea Beetle Class, Potato Foliar Chewing Damage Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Foliar Shot-Hole Damage & Beetle Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Foliar shot-holes easily distinguished; underground grub grooving on tubers can overlap with cutworm chewing.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Pest Bulletins; Indian Journal of Entomology

Symptoms: General pale yellowish-green chlorosis starting uniformly across older lower leaves, moving upward; stunted vine growth, thin erect stems, smaller leaflets, reduced canopy cover.
Required_Dataset: Academic Plant Nutrient Deficiency Datasets, ICAR Soil Health Image Collections
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Foliar Color Index Classifier + Canopy Multi-Level Comparison
Diagnostic_Limitations: Can mimic waterlogging, root rot, or sulfur deficiency; distinguished by progressive bottom-up uniform chlorosis without necrotic patterns.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Mineral Nutrition Guide; Fertiliser Association of India (FAI) Diagnostic Compendium

Symptoms: Dark blue-green or bronzed foliage; margins and tips of older leaves develop chlorotic yellowing followed by crisp brown necrotic marginal scorching and downward curling of leaflet edges.
Required_Dataset: Plant Nutrient Deficiency Repositories, Field Crop Pathology Datasets
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Marginal Necrosis Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Marginal scorching can be confused with leafhopper hopper-burn or saline irrigation injury; lack of insects and uniform marginal necrosis confirms K deficiency.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Technical Bulletin on Potato Soil Fertility; SDAU Banaskantha Soil Testing Advisory

Symptoms: Stunted, rigid, spindly plants; foliage turns dull, dark matte-green; leaf margins curl upward with purplish-bronze pigmentation on abaxial surfaces; delayed tuber bulking.
Required_Dataset: University Plant Pathology Nutrition Libraries, Kaggle Nutrient Disorder Sets
Detection_Method: Foliar Anthocyanin / Pigmentation Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Purpling of stems and leaves can also be triggered by cold soil temperatures in north Gujarat winter; soil pH and temperature context helps.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Nutrition Handbook; Gujarat State Department of Agriculture Soil Advisory

Scientific_Name: Physiological Disorder (High Soil Temp / Ca Imbalance)
Symptoms: Irregular, dry, corky light-brown to reddish-brown necrotic spots or flecks scattered throughout internal tuber flesh, primarily within the vascular ring; skin and periderm completely healthy and blemish-free.
Required_Dataset: Internal Tuber Defect Cross-Section Images, University Storage Pathology Sets
Detection_Method: Cut-Tuber Cross-Section Semantic Segmentation / X-Ray NIR (Not possible from intact tuber)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Completely invisible from exterior intact tuber photographs; user must slice tuber across center to provide cross-section photograph.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Physiological Disorders in Potato; Banaskantha Cold Storage Association Review

Scientific_Name: Physiological Disorder (Rapid Cell Expansion / Irregular Moisture)
Symptoms: Irregular star-shaped or lens-shaped central internal cavity in the pith of oversized tubers, lined with brown necrotic or white corky tissue; outer skin completely normal.
Required_Dataset: Cross-Sectioned Potato Tuber Internal Defects Dataset
Detection_Method: Cut-Tuber Cross-Section Image Analysis (Not detectable from intact tuber)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Intact tuber exterior shows no symptoms whatever; requires tuber cross-sectional slicing or acoustic/X-ray density transmission.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Post-Harvest Advisory; University of California Davis Postharvest Technology Center

Scientific_Name: Physiological Disorder (Excessive Sunlight Exposure / Shallow Planting)
Symptoms: Intense emerald to olive-green coloration developing on tuber periderm due to chlorophyll synthesis upon exposure to direct or indirect sunlight, accompanied by poisonous glycoalkaloid (solanine) buildup.
Required_Dataset: Tuber Periderm Color Datasets, Mendeley Potato Grading Images, Kaggle Tuber Surface Defects
Detection_Method: HSV / CIELAB Green Hue Segmentation + YOLOv8 Defect Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Easily identified visually; model must alert user regarding toxicity (solanine makes tubers unfit for human or animal consumption).
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Quality Standards; Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Potato Guidelines

Symptoms: Turgid, vibrant deep green foliage with uniform coloration, intact leaf margins, unblemished smooth stems, normal venation, absence of lesions, chlorosis, webbing, or insect feeding.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage Potato Healthy, PlantDoc, CPRI Deesa Verified Clean Field Imagery
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Clean Canopy Classifier / Outlier Filter
Diagnostic_Limitations: Must be validated across multiple lighting conditions and growth stages to prevent false positive disease alerts on healthy mature plants.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CPRI Standard Plant Phenotyping Protocols; ICAR-DIPA Standard Agricultural References

Symptoms: Circular to irregular dark brown to black spots on leaves, rapidly enlarging and merging, causing blighted 'shot-hole' appearance; elongated sunken dark brown stem lesions; sunken circular circular fruit pits oozing salmon-pink gelatinous spore masses under wet weather.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Anthracnose Image Repositories, Mendeley Watermelon Diseases, Kaggle Melon Rots
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Foliar & Fruit Classifier + U-Net Lesion Segmentation
Diagnostic_Limitations: Foliar lesions can resemble Gummy Stem Blight; sunken fruit depressions with pink spore matrices are diagnostic for Anthracnose.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Plant Pathology Bulletin; ICAR-CIAH Cucurbitaceous Crop Manual

Symptoms: Bright yellow, chlorotic, angular lesions sharply delimited by leaf veins on upper leaf surface ('checkerboard pattern'); purplish-gray to blackish downy felt-like sporulation on corresponding lower leaf surface during high humidity; leaves curl inward, scorch brown, and die.
Required_Dataset: PlantDoc Cucurbit, AAU Anand Downy Mildew Dataset, Kaggle Watermelon Foliage
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 / ConvNeXt Angular Lesion Classifier + Dual-Side Foliar Analysis
Diagnostic_Limitations: Angular lesions can be confused with Angular Leaf Spot (bacterial); abaxial purplish-gray sporulation confirms downy mildew.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Research Bulletin; JAU Junagadh Agricultural University Crop Protection Handbook

Symptoms: Distinctive white, powdery, talcum-like circular fungal spots starting on lower older leaves, expanding over upper and lower leaf surfaces, petioles, and young stems; infected foliage turns chlorotic, dull brown, brittle, and withers prematurely; exposed fruit sunscalds.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage, PlantDoc, Cucurbit Powdery Mildew Collections, Gujarat Farm Field Sets
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Powdery Felt Texture Classifier + Color Thresholding
Diagnostic_Limitations: White pesticide spray residues or dried saline water spots can mimic powdery spots; texture density analysis prevents false positive categorization.
Reference_Source: SDAU Department of Plant Pathology; PPQ&S IPM Guidelines for Cucurbits

Symptoms: Unilateral (one-sided) wilting of individual runners/vines during hot afternoons, recovering overnight before permanent vine wilt; golden-brown to reddish vascular discoloration visible in lower taproot and crown tissue when sliced longitudinally.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Vascular Wilt Datasets, AAU Anand Research Station Archives
Detection_Method: Multi-Image Diagnostic Flow (Runner Wilt + Sliced Crown Vascular Browning View)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Aboveground flagging looks identical to bacterial wilt or vine borer; definitive confirmation requires longitudinal slit photo of crown vascular ring.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Vegetable Pathology Bulletins; ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR) Varanasi

Symptoms: Circular dark brown necrotic lesions on leaves beginning at margins with faint concentric zoning; water-soaked tan to bleached stem cankers at nodes, oozing thick amber-reddish gummy exudate; tiny black specks (pycnidia) embedded in cankered tissue.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Gummy Stem Datasets, AAU Vegetable Pathology Imagery
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Stem Canker & Gummy Exudate Detection / Foliar Blight Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Amber gummy ooze at stem nodes is highly distinctive; without stem imagery, foliar lesions alone may be misdiagnosed as Anthracnose or Alternaria.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Plant Pathology Bulletin; University of Florida IFAS Extension Cucurbit Guide

Symptoms: Small circular chlorotic spots on leaves expanding into circular brown necrotic spots (0.5 to 2 cm) with prominent concentric rings and chlorotic halos; spots coalesce causing extensive leaf curling, cupping, and defoliation.
Required_Dataset: PlantDoc, Cucurbit Leaf Spot Datasets, Kaggle Agricultural Plant Health
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Target-Board Lesion Classifier + U-Net Segmentation
Diagnostic_Limitations: Strong similarity to Cercospora leaf spot; concentric target-board circles distinguish Alternaria lesions.
Reference_Source: ICAR-IIVR Varanasi; SDAU Cucurbit Pathology Technical Bulletins

Symptoms: Small, discrete, circular to subcircular spots (2 to 5 mm) with pale grayish-white or tan centers and dark purplish-brown to black borders; leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely; fruits not directly infected.
Required_Dataset: PlantDoc Cercospora Class, Cucurbit Leaf Spot Datasets, University Pathology Vaults
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2-M White-Center Spot Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Distinguished from Alternaria by smaller size and bright white/ash-gray center surrounded by dark purple ring.
Reference_Source: JAU Junagadh Pathology Advisory; AAU Agricultural Extension Bulletins

Symptoms: Water-soaked dark green lesions on leaves rapidly turning brown; dark water-soaked constriction of crown and vines ('damping off' of mature vines); melon fruit develops large water-soaked sunken greasy areas rapidly covered by dense white yeast-like powdered sporangia.
Required_Dataset: Phytophthora Cucurbit Rot Dataset, Kaggle Melon Postharvest Pathology
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Fruit Wet-Rot Detector + White Sporangia Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Fruit rot symptoms unmistakable when powdered white sporangia develop on greasy rind; early foliar blight resembles downy mildew collapse.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CIAH Bikaner Arid Cucurbits Compendium; AAU Vegetable Research Reports

Symptoms: Water-soaked lesions at crown level near soil line under high heat (>35°C) and water stress; stem base turns light tan or bleached silvery-gray, densely speckled with thousands of tiny black pinhead-sized microsclerotia beneath epidermis; vascular collapse.
Required_Dataset: Charcoal Rot Agricultural Image Datasets, Semi-Arid Pathology Archives
Detection_Method: Macro Stem Texture Analysis (Microsclerotial Stippling Detector)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Bleached stem base resembles Gummy Stem Blight; detection requires close-up macro imaging of tiny charcoal microsclerotia peeking through epidermis.
Reference_Source: SDAU Sardarkrushinagar Soil Microbiology Series; ICAR-CAZRI Jodhpur Bulletins

Scientific_Name: Acidovorax citrulli (syn. Acidovorax avenae subsp. citrulli)
Symptoms: Small water-soaked greasy olive-green streaks on seedling cotyledons; on maturing fruit, large dark olive-green water-soaked greasy blotches (10 to 30 cm) with irregular margins appearing on upper fruit surface; rind cracks with amber bacterial exudate.
Required_Dataset: Bacterial Fruit Blotch Special Image Repositories, University Cucurbit Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Greasy Fruit Blotched Pattern Detection + Mask R-CNN
Diagnostic_Limitations: Foliar seedling lesions are subtle and easily missed; fruit blotch symptoms are striking, definitive, and visually pathognomonic on rind.
Reference_Source: EPPO Quarantine Data Sheet; Directorate of PPQ&S Seed Health Testing Guidelines

Symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular lesions delimited by leaf veins; during humid mornings, whitish bacterial tear-drop exudate crusts on lesion underside; dry lesions turn gray-brown, tear away and fall out, giving leaves a ragged 'shot-hole' appearance.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Bacterial Leaf Spot Repositories, PlantDoc Agricultural Datasets
Detection_Method: Angular Lesion Boundary & Tearing Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Closely mimics Downy Mildew angular chlorosis; distinguished by shot-hole tearing of dried lesions and absence of purplish-gray downy sporulation.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Plant Pathology Advisory; CABI Plantwise Knowledge Bank

Symptoms: Foliar mosaic with alternating dark and light green patches, vein banding, puckering, rugose leaf distortion; plant stunting; fruit develops mottled coloration, chlorotic rings, and bumpy raised green warts on rind.
Required_Dataset: PlantVillage, PlantDoc, AAU Anand Cucurbit Virology Archives
Detection_Method: ConvNeXt Foliar Mosaic & Fruit Warting Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Symptom overlap with CMV and Papaya Ringspot Virus; serological/RT-PCR testing needed for definitive strain distinction; CV flags 'Cucurbit Mosaic Complex'.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Plant Virology Research Station; ICAR-IIVR Cucurbit Viral Diseases

Symptoms: Prominent yellow-green foliar mottle, down-curling of leaf margins, severe vine stunting; in advanced stages, leaves become extremely narrow and strap-like ('shoestring symptom'); reduced fruit size with mottled rind.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Virology Collections, PlantDoc, Kaggle Agricultural Viruses
Detection_Method: Shoestring Morphology & Chlorotic Stippling Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Shoestring leaves visually diagnostic in late stages; early mottle cannot be definitively separated from WMV without laboratory serology.
Reference_Source: ICAR-IIVR Varanasi; SDAU Sardarkrushinagar Department of Horticulture

Symptoms: Dark green vein banding, leaf enations (leaf-like outgrowths on abaxial leaf veins), blister-like malformations, leaf distortion; transmission via cucumber beetles and seed.
Required_Dataset: Academic Comovirus Repositories, University Cucurbit Disease Collections
Detection_Method: Foliar Enation & Blister Feature Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Enations and vein blisters are distinctive, but presence is inconsistent across commercial hybrids; field confirmation relies on ELISA.
Reference_Source: CABI Compendium; EPPO Data Sheets on Quarantine Pests

Scientific_Name: Papaya Ringspot Virus Type W (formerly WMV-1, Potyvirus)
Symptoms: Intense foliar yellow mosaic, vein-clearing, severe leaf laminae reduction leading to filiform strap-like leaves; fruit severely malformed with prominent raised bumpy dark-green knobby warts.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Potyvirus Image Vaults, AAU Plant Virology Collections
Detection_Method: Knobby Fruit Wart & Foliar Distortive Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Knobby warts on fruit rind strongly point to PRSV-W; foliar symptoms visually coalesce with WMV and CMV.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Research Publications; Indian Phytopathology Journal

Symptoms: Pre-emergence rotting of seeds; post-emergence water-soaked brown constriction of seedling collar and hypocotyl at soil level; seedling topples over while foliage remains green; taproot soft, brown, and decayed.
Required_Dataset: Damping Off & Seedling Disease Repositories, ICAR Nursery Disease Sets
Detection_Method: Seedling Hypocotyl Constriction & Collar Rot Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Diagnosis requires close-up image of seedling crown and soil interface; cannot be determined from top-down canopy view alone.
Reference_Source: ICAR-IIVR Nursery Disease Management; SDAU Plant Pathology Guide

Symptoms: Dense clusters of small, pale to dark olive-green aphids on young shoots and undersides of leaves; leaves curl downward tightly, cup, and crinkle; heavy sticky honeydew deposits colonized by black sooty mold.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Aphid Dataset, PlantDoc, Kaggle Agricultural Pests
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Aphid Cluster & Foliar Downward Curling Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: High visual detectability; vector for WMV, CMV, and PRSV; advisory must focus on early economic threshold before viral inoculation.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Entomology Department; SDAU Vegetable Pest Management Series

Symptoms: Tiny white flying adults fluttering from vine canopy when agitated; translucent oval scale-like nymphs adhering to abaxial leaf surface; leaf silvering/chlorosis, sooty mold, vector of Begomoviruses (Watermelon Chlorotic Stunt).
Required_Dataset: IP102 Whitefly Dataset, Cotton & Cucurbit Whitefly Repositories
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Abaxial Nymph & Adult Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Requires photographing under-leaf surface where colonies congregate; upper leaf shows only indirect sooty mold and chlorosis.
Reference_Source: PPQ&S Cucurbit Pest Management Package; JAU Junagadh Entomology Bulletins

Symptoms: Bright orange-red, oblong, shiny chrysomelid beetles (6 to 8 mm) actively feeding on leaves; chew characteristic circular or semi-circular feeding holes and rings in cotyledons and foliage, resulting in skeletonized leaves.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Red Pumpkin Beetle Class, ICAR-CIAH Cucurbit Beetle Imagery
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Beetle Detection + Circular Foliar Notch Pattern Recognizer
Diagnostic_Limitations: Highly distinctive; beetle color and circular feeding rings have zero visual overlap with other Gujarat watermelon pests.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Agricultural Entomology Bulletin; SDAU Banaskantha Pest Calendar

Symptoms: Female fruit fly punctures tender developing fruit skin to lay eggs; tiny puncture spots ooze translucent amber resinous fluid; fruit develops sunken deformity, rot, premature yellowing, and interior liquefaction packed with white jumping maggots.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Fruit Fly Dataset, ICAR Tephritidae Collections, Melon Damage Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Oviposition Puncture & Fruit Deformity Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Early oviposition puncture hole requires sharp close-up fruit photograph; fruit deformity and rotting secondary decay easily detected.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CIAH Bikaner IPM Guidelines; AAU Anand Entomology Advisory

Symptoms: Leaves cup upward with wavy crinkled margins; lower leaf surface takes on silvery-bronzed specular sheen dotted with tiny dark fecal frass spots; growing vine tips become stunted, bunched, and brittle ('rosette appearance').
Required_Dataset: IP102 Thrips Class, Micro-Pest Repositories, Cucurbit Thrips Damage Sets
Detection_Method: Silvery Foliar Bronzing & Upward Cupping Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Insect bodies minute (0.8-1 mm); detection relies primarily on distinct upward cupping, silvery sheen, and shoot tip rosette formation.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Entomological Reports; JAU Junagadh Vegetable Crop Advisory

Symptoms: Fine pale-yellow to white stippling and speckled chlorotic dots on upper leaf surface; under-leaf shows dense, fine silken webbing harboring tiny reddish-brown crawling mites; leaves turn dirty yellow, bronze, dry up, and drop.
Required_Dataset: PlantDoc Spider Mite Class, IP102 Tetranychidae, Kaggle Mite Damage Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Webbing & Foliar Stippling Pattern Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Fine stippling easily confused with early thrips damage; presence of fine silken webbing on abaxial surface confirms spider mites.
Reference_Source: SDAU Department of Entomology; PPQ&S Acarology Advisory

Symptoms: Conspicuous, slender, white to translucent serpentine winding mines and wandering tunnels meandering irregularly across leaf lamina; black frass trail visible within mine; heavy mining causes complete foliar drying.
Required_Dataset: PlantDoc, IP102 Leafminer Class, Kaggle Serpentine Mine Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 / Mask R-CNN Serpentine Trail Segmentation
Diagnostic_Limitations: Completely unmistakable visually; serpentine trail geometric structure provides >98% computer vision classification confidence.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Entomology Bulletin; ICAR-IIVR Insect Pest Compendium

Symptoms: Bright green caterpillar with two longitudinal white stripes along dorsal surface; rolls and webs leaves together while skeletonizing foliage; bores clean round entry holes into developing melon fruit, extruding wet white-yellow frass.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Diaphania Class, Cucurbit Fruit Borer Image Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Larval & Fruit Borehole Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Larva easily detected on leaves; fruit borehole requires photographing the puncture site and frass deposit.
Reference_Source: JAU Junagadh Agriculture Bulletin; SDAU Entomology Field Guide

Symptoms: Newly transplanted or germinated watermelon vines cleanly cut off at soil surface overnight; wilting detached runners lying on ground; nocturnal gray-brown larva curled up beneath nearby clods of soil.
Required_Dataset: IP102 Noctuid Cutworm Sets, Cucurbit Nursery Damage Images
Detection_Method: Stem Severance Classifier + Larva Detection
Diagnostic_Limitations: Severed runner damage visible; finding and photographing the concealed subterranean larva in soil confirms pest identity.
Reference_Source: PPQ&S Cucurbit Package of Practices; AAU Anand Entomology Advisory

Symptoms: Severe knot-like, swollen galls and beads on taproot and secondary roots; plant vines severely stunted, yellowing, and wilting during hot midday hours despite adequate soil moisture; delayed fruiting and fruit undersizing.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Root Nematode Gall Datasets, Academic Nematology Archives
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Root Swelling & Gall Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Aboveground wilting looks identical to Fusarium wilt or moisture stress; requires uprooting washed root system photograph showing root galls.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Department of Nematology; ICAR-CPRI/CIAH Nematology Bulletins

Symptoms: Uniform pale-yellow chlorosis beginning on older crown leaves and slowly advancing toward growing vine tips; vine growth slow, runners thin and spindly; undersized pale fruits.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Nutrition Image Datasets, ICAR Arid Horticulture Nutritional Sets
Detection_Method: Foliar Color Gradient & Canopy Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Requires seeing overall canopy distribution (bottom-up chlorosis) to distinguish from iron deficiency (which affects youngest top leaves).
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Soil Health Bulletins; University of Florida IFAS Watermelon Nutrition

Symptoms: Marginal chlorosis on older leaves progressing to bronze necrotic scorching along leaf edges while central leaf blade remains green; fruits develop tapered blossom end with bulbous stem end ('bottle-necked fruit').
Required_Dataset: Plant Nutrient Deficiency Datasets, Watermelon Fruit Grading Libraries
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Marginal Scorching & Bottle-Neck Fruit Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Marginal leaf scorch can resemble saline irrigation burn; combination of marginal scorch with misshapen tapered fruit confirms K deficiency.
Reference_Source: SDAU Soil Science Compendium; Indian Society of Soil Science Technical Bulletins

Symptoms: Striking, distinct interveinal chlorosis on older and mid-canopy leaves: areas between major leaf veins turn bright yellow or creamy white, while veins themselves remain distinctly dark green; leaves become brittle.
Required_Dataset: Foliar Deficiency Repositories, Agricultural University Pathology Images
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Interveinal Chlorosis Pattern Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Strong visual separation due to green vein retention; very common in coarse sandy soils of Sabarkantha and Banaskantha watermelon tracts.
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Micronutrient Research Station Bulletins; FAI Diagnostics

Symptoms: Young expanding leaves at vine tips become severely cupped, distorted, with scorched, hooked downward margins; growing tips die back ('dieback'); directly triggers Blossom End Rot in developing melons.
Required_Dataset: Cucurbit Physiological Disorder Datasets, Academic Plant Nutrition
Detection_Method: Vine Tip Curvature & Meristem Distortion Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Apical leaf distortion mimics viral infection or herbicide drift; presence of blossom end rot on nearby fruit confirms calcium failure.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CIAH Bikaner Vegetable Bulletin; UC Davis IPM Cucurbit Disorders

Symptoms: Small water-soaked lesion at blossom end (distal tip) of developing fruit, enlarging into a large, flat, sunken, leathery, dark brown to black dry necrotic patch; secondary fungi may colonize necrotic spot.
Required_Dataset: Watermelon Fruit Defect Datasets, Kaggle Blossom End Rot, University Datasets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Distal Fruit Lesion Detector + Texture Segmentation
Diagnostic_Limitations: Location on blossom end is pathognomonic; distinct from Anthracnose (which causes circular pits across entire fruit rind).
Reference_Source: AAU Anand Horticulture Extension Bulletins; ICAR-IIVR Varanasi Advisory

Symptoms: Circular to irregular bleached, grayish-white or creamy-tan paper-thin, dry, sunken necrotic area on the sun-exposed upper surface of watermelon fruit due to loss of canopy foliage; fruit flesh underneath becomes watery and flavorless.
Required_Dataset: Sunscald Agricultural Image Libraries, Melon Postharvest Defect Sets
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Upper Rind Bleaching Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Confined exclusively to upper sun-exposed surface; distinguished from bacterial fruit blotch by dry bleached papery texture vs greasy dark green water-soaking.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CIAH Arid Cucurbit Production Technology; SDAU Horticulture Department

Symptoms: Longitudinal or burst radial fissures and splits tearing through watermelon rind exposing inner red/yellow flesh; occurs when heavy irrigation or rain follows prolonged dry spell during rapid fruit enlargement.
Required_Dataset: Watermelon Fruit Grading & Rind Burst Datasets, Kaggle Agricultural Quality
Detection_Method: YOLOv8 Rind Fissure & Flesh Exposure Detector
Diagnostic_Limitations: Visual diagnosis unmistakable; model must provide preventive water regulation and mulching advisories.
Reference_Source: JAU Junagadh Agricultural Extension Guide; AAU Anand Horticulture Bulletins

Scientific_Name: Physiological Disorder (Inadequate Pollination / Rapid Cell Expansion)
Symptoms: Internal triangular, star-shaped, or radial fissure/gap separating the three internal carpels within fruit flesh; fruit exterior remains completely intact, unblemished, and visually normal.
Required_Dataset: Cross-Sectioned Watermelon Internal Quality Datasets
Detection_Method: Cut-Fruit Cross-Section Analysis / Acoustic Density Sensor (Not diagnosable from intact fruit)
Diagnostic_Limitations: Zero external visual symptoms on intact fruit; requires cutting melon open or using non-destructive acoustic tapping / ultrasonic transmission.
Reference_Source: University of Delaware Extension Hollow Heart Review; ICAR-CIAH Technical Circular

Symptoms: Vigorous, sprawling vines with deep-green deeply lobed foliage, clean yellow flowers, vibrant unblemished tendrils, healthy developing melons with uniform rind patterns and no lesion or pest damage.
Required_Dataset: Clean Cucurbit Field Repositories, AAU Anand Healthy Crop Imagery
Detection_Method: EfficientNetV2 Healthy Canopy Baseline Classifier
Diagnostic_Limitations: Requires multi-lighting baseline to avoid misclassifying natural leaf lobing or pale vein variegation in specific cultivars as virus mosaic.
Reference_Source: ICAR-CIAH Cucurbit Phenotyping Protocols; Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) Standards
